name: Immer
overview: Immer was a male Levite and a priest known in the post-exilic period. He is notably recognized as the father of Meshillemith and served in the priestly duties during the restoration of Israel. His role as a Levite priest places him within the sacred lineage responsible for temple service.
namesAndTitles: The name Immer means "lamb," a proper name mentioned in 1 Chronicles 9:12. This name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a simple, meaningful designation within the Hebrew context.
familyAndRelationships: Immer was the father of Meshillemith, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:12. He was a descendant of Aaron, linking him to the priestly line, and had ancestors named Hanani and Zebadiah mentioned in Ezra 10:20. Scripture thus situates him within a notable Levitical family lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Immer's significance lies in his priestly service during Israel's return from exile, as noted in Ezra and Nehemiah. His role underscores the continuity of the Aaronic priesthood and the restoration of proper worship in Jerusalem. Being listed among the priests who returned highlights his part in reestablishing the covenant community under God's guidance.
